scope: Resolve implementation readiness for 7BH.3 future-output filename collisions across Windows, Linux/ext4, and Apple filesystems; document the observed local gap without retaining an ASCII-only workaround.

method.kind: Primary platform documentation review plus local bounded CLI reproduction
method.localObservation: The existing batch preflight admitted CaseCollision.dwg and casecollision.dxf on a Darwin case-insensitive output volume. The two normalized output names alias under that directory's filename behavior. The temporary ASCII-fold/case-probe prototype was removed because it did not meet the existing plan's native-equivalence requirement.

evidence.observed: Microsoft documents a per-directory FILE_CASE_SENSITIVE_INFORMATION flag and a query API. Windows/WSL documentation describes per-directory behavior and an inheritance exception in WSL 1.
doesNotEstablish: case behavior for every filesystem provider or remote share
short-name/trailing-dot-space alias closure from the case flag alone
that a temporary child directory always shares the output parent's collation
evidence.planUse: Query the actual directory with a supported native API; model path aliases separately; treat unsupported providers or unavailable state explicitly.

evidence.observed: The kernel documents case-insensitive lookup as per-directory and dependent on a filesystem-wide casefold feature/encoding. Its documented comparison uses canonical decomposition and a Unicode-versioned encoding; invalid-name behavior can fall back when strict mode is absent. EXT4_CASEFOLD_FL is the relevant directory flag.
doesNotEstablish: that all Linux filesystems are case-sensitive or use ext4 rules
that lexical UTF-8 comparison matches every mount/provider
that the current host's Darwin result qualifies Linux behavior
evidence.planUse: Query ext4 directory and encoding capabilities where supported; define invalid input handling; fail closed for unknown filesystem or mount semantics.

evidence.observed: Apple documents case-sensitive and case-insensitive APFS variants and exposes volumeSupportsCaseSensitiveNames. Its archived APFS FAQ describes normalization-insensitive names in both variants and Unicode 9.0 behavior for the documented APFS generation. Apple separately warns that systems may use filesystems other than APFS.
doesNotEstablish: current name-comparison details for every macOS version and volume provider
that case sensitivity alone captures APFS normalization equivalence
HFS+, network filesystem, or other provider behavior
evidence.planUse: Query the actual volume/provider and verify the documented normalization profile applies before using it; do not infer from host OS or APFS-only facts.

implementationReadiness.targetComplexity: O(n log n) or comparably bounded for up to 10000 planned outputs
fastValidation: generated case/normalization/provider alias controls with no added CTest registration
one bounded 10000-name comparator/index control after implementation
